correctness.rationale: For p^a, phi(p^a)sigma(p^a)=p^(a-1)(p^(a+1)-1), so v_p=a-1. For squarefree pq with p 18. If q>p then q|Phi_3(p); setting Phi_3(p)=qt and using q≡±1(mod p), the + branch yields 0 t=1; the minus branch for odd p yields t=p-1 even against odd Phi_3(p). Thus exact classification and converse hold for all n with Omega<=3; no inference from finite tests is required.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge PASS for the exact restricted statement. The natural residue-one form of OEIS A056100 and exact product A062354 are prior data, not a theorem classifying all n with at most three prime factors. Broughan–Ford–Luca 2013 treat equality phi(n)sigma(n)=m^2 and n-m=a via Pell-type techniques; that hypothesis neither states nor implies n|phi(n)sigma(n) in the Omega<=3 range. Source searches for aliases p^2 q and Phi_3(p) found no covering infinite family; absence from search is not proof of priority.
